title: Control plane certificate chain mismatch causing agent join failures after private upgrade
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During the 2026-02 private cluster control plane upgrade, a subset of private agents failed to fully join the control plane. Failures manifested as repeated TLS handshake rejections citing certificate chain validation errors. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, immediate mitigations, and medium-term action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-14 02:10 UTC - upgrade started; 02:28 UTC - first agent join failures observed; 02:35 UTC - mitigations (pause rollout, revert cert bundle) attempted; 03:12 UTC - temporary hotfix deployed on control plane CA trust store; 03:45 UTC - majority of agents rejoined; 06:00 UTC - rollout resumed with adjusted cert handling; incident declared mitigated at 08:10 UTC.
root_cause: A staged change to the control plane CA bundle altered the certificate chain path ordering. Several older agent builds perform strict chain validation and expect specific intermediate ordering; the new ordering caused validation to fail even though certificates were otherwise valid. The release test matrix did not include older agent versions present in several private deployments, exposing a compatibility gap.
mitigation: Rolled back the CA bundle ordering to the previous canonical chain on affected control planes and pushed a hotfix that accepts multiple chain permutations while preserving strict validation for unknown roots. We paused the automated rollout for 24 hours and coordinated with customers running older agent versions.
action_items: Create a compatibility test matrix that includes last three stable agent releases and run CA bundle reorder permutations during preflight (owner: Infra QA, estimate: 5)
Add automated acceptance tests in the upgrade pipeline to validate agent join across known agent versions and certificate chain permutations (owner: Runtime, estimate: 8)
Document and publish a Control Plane CA bundle change runbook with clear rollback steps and a checklist for verifying agent compatibility (owner: SRE, estimate: 3)
Implement instrumentation to alert when a significant fraction (>5%) of agents report TLS validation errors within a rolling 10-minute window (owner: Observability, estimate: 5)
Backfill customer inventory to identify private deployments running agent versions older than 2025-11 and proactively schedule upgrade assistance (owner: Customer Success, estimate: 8)

Prototype tolerant chain validation layer for older agents to accept canonical permutations while maintaining strict root verification; ship as opt-in flag in next agent release (owner: Runtime, estimate: 8)
Post-mortem review with Security to validate that hotfix preserved PKI guarantees and to sign off on long-term approach (owner: Security, estimate: 2)
Update upgrade gating policy to require at least one successful canary with older-agent configurations in target customer snapshots (owner: Platform, estimate: 3)
comments: 2026-02-15 Marcus Chen: Initial RCA draft completed; sharing with SRE and Security for review.
2026-02-18 SRE: Confirmed rollback procedure; created runbook draft (link above).
2026-02-22 Security: Performed quick audit of the hotfix; no root compromise found; recommended longer-term chain-tolerant approach.
2026-02-28 QA: Added permutation tests to nightly pipeline; identified two more permutations to include.
2026-03-05 Product: Customer Success outreach plan approved; scheduled upgrade assistance for 6 customers with legacy agents.
